notes: Both tools are listed unconditionally by the ListTools handler with no toolset/flag gating (dist/index.js:215-217).
Rate limiting (dist/index.js:82-94) can cause errors but does not change reachability or labels.
Error paths echo the Brave API response body back to the agent (dist/index.js:121, 148, 174, 191), another vendor-controlled text channel but still not attacker-chosen destinations.

brave_local_search.rationale: `performLocalSearch` returns Brave POI names, addresses and `descData.descriptions` text (third-party/community-sourced business listing content) to the agent, and falls back to `performWebSearch` which returns arbitrary web content, so UNTRUSTED. All fetches target the fixed Brave endpoints (`/res/v1/web/search`, `/res/v1/local/pois`, `/res/v1/local/descriptions`) with only the query/ids parameters, so no agent-chosen destination and hence no SINK. Nothing non-public from the host or the user's accounts is returned, so no SECRET.

brave_web_search.rationale: `performWebSearch` fetches Brave web search results and returns attacker-influenceable `title`, `description` and `url` fields from arbitrary web pages straight into the agent context, so results are UNTRUSTED. The request goes only to the fixed vendor endpoint `https://api.search.brave.com/res/v1/web/search` with agent-supplied text limited to the `q` query parameter, which is a fixed-vendor query rather than an attacker-readable destination, so it is not a SINK. No local files, credentials or intranet data are read back (the `BRAVE_API_KEY` is only sent as a header, never returned), so no SECRET, and there is no code execution.

value_conditions.effect: If unset, the server prints an error and exits before serving any tools, so both tools become unavailable; when set, both tools are advertised unconditionally.
